cases.description: A newly created JsonSchema instance (constructed via the public static factory `JsonSchema.from` with an empty schema) should have its `requiredValidator` field unset. Calling `getRequiredValidator()` must return `null`.

A schema that defines a required property list should cause the JsonSchema instance to create and store a RequiredValidator. After the schema is parsed (via JsonSchemaFactory) the call to getRequiredValidator() must return a non‑null object of type RequiredValidator.

A schema without a "required" keyword (but with other validators such as a type validator) must leave the requiredValidator field unset. After initialization getRequiredValidator() should still return null.
Calling getRequiredValidator() multiple times on the same JsonSchema must return the exact same RequiredValidator object (i.e., the method does not create a new instance on each call).

cases.expected: referenced schema returns non‑null RequiredValidator, referring schema returns null
cases.description: When a schema contains a $ref that points to another schema which defines required properties, the RequiredValidator is created only for the resolved (referenced) JsonSchema instance. The JsonSchema that only holds the $ref should not have a requiredValidator of its own.

group: JsonSchema.getRequiredValidator() - required keyword with empty array

cases.description: An explicit but empty "required" array still triggers the creation of a RequiredValidator (it will simply validate that no properties are required). The getter must therefore return a non‑null validator.
